write_path_trace.question: Where does SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS.json actually get written, and why does the existing sanitize_payload_for_output call at run_extraction_v5.py:2624 not cover it?
write_path_trace.answer_summary: The packet's premise was ALMOST right but not exactly right, and the correction matters. The write path IS covered by sanitize_payload_for_output. The real gap is that sanitize_payload_for_output is the WEAKER of the two existing scrubs.
trace: STEP 1 - Where the artifact is written. C8's four RISK_LOCATIONS artifacts are model outputs, not prescan outputs. Each partition's raw LLM response lands at <phase_dir>/raw/<step_id>__<partition_id>.json. normalize_step() (run_extraction_v5.py, def at :8521) then reads every raw partition file, calls extract_artifacts_from_partition_payload() (:8332), buckets items by artifact_name, merges the per-partition chunks via merge_json_chunks(), and writes the merged artifact to <phase_dir>/norm/<artifact_name> at run_extraction_v5.py:8708-8712 (pre-change line numbers). That single site is the only write path for the non-.partX JSON norm artifacts; .partX artifacts take the adjacent branch a few lines above. Verified by grep: SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS is a data value flowing through artifact_name, never a literal in the runtime source - which is why 'grep SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS run_extraction_v5.py' returns nothing and made the gap look larger than it is.

STEP 2 - What already protects it. That write goes through write_json() (run_extraction_v5.py:2620-2637), which applies sanitize_payload_for_output() to EVERY artifact payload (and sanitize_payload_for_failed_sidecar for *.FAILED.json). So the claim in the packet invariant that 'SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS is NOT referenced anywhere in output_safety.py or the artifact write path' is literally true as a grep result but MISLEADING as a security conclusion: the artifact write path was never unprotected. Reported here plainly rather than quietly inventing work around it.

STEP 3 - The actual gap. output_safety.py ships two scrub strengths over the SAME regex set. sanitize_text_for_output() applies _PRIVATE_KEY_BLOCK_RE, _SECRET_QUERY_RE, _AUTH_HEADER_RE, _SECRET_ASSIGN_RE, _BEARER_INLINE_RE and _PROVIDER_TOKEN_RE. sanitize_text_for_provider_payload() applies all of those PLUS _LONG_TOKEN_CANDIDATE_RE (output_safety.py:37-39), the high-entropy catch-all for any 40+ char mixed-case-plus-digit token that is not a hex digest. So a secret survives the artifact write path iff it (a) carries no recognizable sensitive key name adjacent to it, and (b) has no known provider prefix. That is exactly a raw AWS secret ACCESS KEY VALUE - as opposed to its AKIA/ASIA-prefixed access key ID, which _PROVIDER_TOKEN_RE does catch. It is also exactly what a non-compliant model produces when it obeys C8's exact-<=200-char-excerpt Evidence Rule and ignores R3-004's redaction carve-out, because the excerpt it copies is a bare source line.

STEP 4 - Empirical confirmation (not assumed). For the fake bare secret 'TqZ8bKp3Vn6Ws0Ad5Ef2Gh7Rt8Yc3Lm2Kf9Qx4Mn6Op1Zr7' embedded in the excerpt 'credential_blob <SECRET>': sanitize_text_for_output returns it UNCHANGED; sanitize_text_for_provider_payload returns 'credential_blob [REDACTED]'. Reproduced directly in-process against the shipped module before any code was changed.

STEP 5 - Downstream blast radius. PROMPT_R11_SECURITY_RISK_SYNTHESIS.md:18,126,128 consumes SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS.json from C8 as an input artifact, so anything that lands in the norm artifact is re-sent to a paid provider during R11 synthesis. C9 (PROMPT_C9:38,188) also loads it read-only. That is the leak chain R3-004 named and could not close from the prompt layer.
write_path_trace.verdict: GENUINELY UNCOVERED - but narrower and more precise than the packet premise. Not a missing scrub; a scrub of insufficient strength for this specific artifact class. Fixed by selecting the stricter existing scrub for a named artifact set, with no new regexes.

output_safety.py: Added SECURITY_SENSITIVE_ARTIFACT_NAMES (frozenset) naming the seven artifacts whose contract forbids any secret value on disk: SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS.json (C8), HOME_KEYS_SURFACE.json + HOME_REFERENCES.json (H1), HOME_SQLITE_SCHEMA.json (H7), M3_CONPORT_EXPORT_SAFE.json, M4_DOPE_CONTEXT_EXPORT_SAFE.json, M5_MCP_HEALTH_EXPORT_SAFE.json (M safe-exports). The set is exactly the six prompts R3-004 made binding, expanded to their declared outputs; artifact names were read out of promptsets/v4/promptset.yaml rather than guessed.
Added is_security_sensitive_artifact(name) - basename-normalized membership test, so a path-qualified name resolves identically.

Added sanitize_payload_for_security_artifact(payload) - a thin delegation to the EXISTING sanitize_payload_for_provider. NO new regex was authored: this reuses _SECRET_PATTERNS as-is, per the packet invariant and so that TP-RTE-TRUTH-D-004 (which consolidates the existing two regex copies) is not made harder. The docstring states why the provider-grade scrub is the right one (it is strictly stronger, adding only _LONG_TOKEN_CANDIDATE_RE).
A block comment records the write-path trace above at the point of use, so the next reader does not have to re-derive why the generic scrub was insufficient.
run_extraction_v5.py: normalize_step(): at the single norm-artifact JSON write site, the merged payload is passed through sanitize_payload_for_security_artifact() when the artifact name is in the security set, BEFORE write_json(). write_json's generic scrub still runs afterwards, so the change is additive and strictly hardening - no artifact gets less scrubbing than before.
change_summary.why_this_is_enforcement_and_not_instruct: The scrub runs on the merged payload after the model has spoken and before any bytes reach disk. It is unconditional for the named artifacts, requires no model cooperation, and cannot be talked out of by prompt injection or jailbreak, because the model never gets a vote at this seam. R3-004's binding prompt rule is preserved and remains the first line of defense (it also keeps secrets out of the RAW partition files, which this change does not touch - see residual risks).
change_summary.finding_preservation: Masking is span-level, never row-level. path, line_range, risk_type, affected_symbol, exposure_vector, the evidence[].path/line_range, and the surrounding excerpt text all survive; only the secret literal becomes [REDACTED]. Asserted explicitly, including that the item count stays 1 - the location IS the value, and dropping a finding would be a worse outcome than the leak it prevents.

observed_not_fixed.impact: A bare high-entropy secret can still land in raw/. It does NOT reach the norm artifact or R11 synthesis, which is what F-23 named as the leak chain. Raw is the model's verbatim response and is intentionally the least-transformed surface. Hardening it is a wider behavioral change (it would alter every phase's raw bytes and could move goldens) and belongs in its own packet.

residual_risks: COVERAGE IS BY ARTIFACT NAME, NOT BY CONTENT. A new secret-bearing artifact added to the promptset will not be scrubbed until its name is added to SECURITY_SENSITIVE_ARTIFACT_NAMES. This is a deliberate trade: content-based detection across all ~136 artifacts would risk mangling legitimate long identifiers repo-wide. Mitigation available to a follow-up: assert set membership against promptset.yaml so a rename or addition fails a test rather than silently losing protection.

THE SCRUB IS REGEX-BOUNDED. A secret shorter than 40 chars, with no provider prefix and no adjacent sensitive key name, still passes. That is a property of the existing shared regex set which this packet reuses by mandate, not a new weakness - and it is why R3-004's prompt-layer rule remains necessary rather than superseded.

OVER-REDACTION IS POSSIBLE IN PRINCIPLE. The provider-grade scrub can mask a legitimate 40+ char mixed-case identifier appearing inside one of the seven artifacts. Hex digests are explicitly exempted by _looks_like_hex_digest. Judged acceptable for exactly this artifact class: these seven exist to record credential LOCATIONS, so a masked long token there is far cheaper than a leaked one. Not applied to any other artifact.
